runtime_pins.dependency_policy: standard library first; pinned Go modules, parser runtime, model adapter, or tool dependency only with task evidence and license review
runtime_pins.distribution_target: explicitly licensed and integrity-signed design-partner binary or source package for consumer-local or consumer-controlled CI execution; public OSS, self-serve, and Homebrew require a separate approved gate
runtime_pins.provider_intent_policy: provider-originated API or SDK update delivery launched through a provider-paid, services-assisted sunset campaign; one accountably confirmed Provider Change Contract is reused by the exact invited cohort, each non-executable provider event binds its exact digest, audience, deadline, and supersession state, and neither contract nor event grants consumer repository authority; a universal registry, elaborate provider PKI, connection receipts, and receipt-backed billing are deferred
runtime_pins.agent_runner_policy: agent_execution_policy defaults to disabled so notify-only, scan-only, and deterministic-only routes require no Agent Runner credential; an agent-assisted route pauses until the API Consumer Organization configures one exact qualified adapter and version, executable source and digest, permitted noninteractive auth mode and entitlement class, and observable actual model route; Codex and Claude Code are launch targets only after common conformance and per-version live canaries, while Cursor is deferred behind the same gate; every attempt resolves the approved executable canonically, rejects repository-local PATH shadowing, and uses a clean ephemeral session with neutral home/config roots; static native instructions are disabled or explicitly selected and digest-bound as untrusted context while executable plugins, MCP servers, and hooks are prohibited; runner host isolation binds mounts, OS credentials, sockets, descriptors, child processes, egress, and cleanup to an exact qualified backend identity and hard CPU, memory, PID/process-tree, disk, and open-file quotas; each agent action freezes one local-runtime, runner-mediated, direct-model, or hybrid topology and its minimum disclosure/network/credential set; consumer_managed is the default configured funding mode, provider_sponsored_lumyn_managed is optional, credential and usage-billing owners are explicit, and no adapter, model, endpoint, credential-owner, or billing-owner fallback is silent
runtime_pins.model_policy: bounded agent use requires agent_execution_policy=configured, exact Agent Runner Vendor, adapter and version, executable source/path/digest, conformance digest, permitted noninteractive auth mode and entitlement class, clean-session identity, funding mode, credential and usage-billing owners, native-configuration digest, observable actual Model Provider, endpoint, model route and version, parameters, prompt and tool digests, selected context and request-disclosure classes, retention and regional posture, separate Agent Runner and model credential environments/scopes and network endpoints/operations, read and write paths, file, line, diff, turn, token, time, retry, concurrency, attempt, and cost budgets, plus normalized request, response, tool-call, edit, usage, error, cancellation, exit, and patch provenance; repository, provider, native-config, tool, runner, and model content is untrusted and cannot widen any boundary; managed credentials bind broker issuer, exact audience and one-hour maximum TTL; one-time broker redemption creates one attempt-scoped session whose in-attempt calls remain within hard token and cost quotas, with no refresh, post-attempt replay, or cross-attempt reuse; revocation and reconciliation use a vendor-native bound credential or approved budget-enforcing proxy
runtime_pins.verification_policy: deterministic repository and workflow verification is independent from deterministic or agent-assisted generation, runs from the exact candidate head in a fresh process and view with frozen command/config digests, no Agent Runner/model credentials, and no generation-owned evidence write handle, under a pinned qualified command-isolation backend with exact mounts/environment, hard resource quotas, inherited child limits, offline/lifecycle defaults, and cleanup evidence; a credential-bearing sandbox entrypoint uses its own exact-head, endpoint-only, teardown/orphan-evidenced isolation profile; verification preserves baseline failures and cannot be satisfied by a model completion or self-verification
runtime_pins.delivery_policy: complete local evidence plus patch, optional local branch, and PR-ready bundle is the fallback; at least one tested draft PR requires separate atomic short-lived non-default-branch-push and draft-PR actions, evidence-bound idempotency, and no auto-merge; generation, verification, branch, and PR routes never become one aggregate authority; manual delivery cannot close automated-delivery acceptance; first-campaign product proof requires one same qualifying run from authenticated event and installed preauthorization through an organically agent-assisted item on a consumer-selected qualified runner, independent exact-head verification, Lumyn-opened draft PR, and provider-received consented status projection; deterministic rerouting cannot manufacture agent proof, and status is event-bound, provenance-labeled, and never inferred from silence
runtime_pins.artifact_namespace: .factory/artifacts contains source-safe Factory controls and separately consented aggregate or digest evidence only; consumer-private code, prompts, responses, agent sessions, patches, traces, credentials, and identifiable campaign evidence use an approved external private root and are never API-provider-visible
runtime_pins.live_work_policy: Factory worker capabilities are only approval, credentials, and network and never substitute for Lumyn product action scopes; consumer installation, event-specific authorization, Agent Runner network, Agent Runner credential, model disclosure, model network, model credential, repository, command, registry, sandbox, GitHub, reporting, retention, and deletion actions are separate, expiring, revocable, fail-closed product grants whose exact route-selected union is frozen before action
runtime_pins.dispatch_policy: factoryd dispatch is paused and fail-closed until the external profiles/lumyn.yaml contract is updated for v3.1 and factoryd is qualified against this regenerated task, authority, model, evidence, and closure generation

locked_decisions: Provider-originated update delivery is the product; a provider-paid, services-assisted sunset campaign is the initial commercial motion.

Execution is consumer-local; agent_execution_policy defaults to disabled for notify-only, scan-only, and deterministic-only routes, while agent-assisted routes require a configured customer-selected qualified bounded Agent Runner.
Codex and Claude Code are launch Agent Runner targets behind one common conformance contract and per-version/executable live canaries; Cursor is deferred behind the same gate.

Every agent attempt resolves an approved executable by canonical path and digest, validates auth mode and entitlement, rejects repository-local PATH shadowing, and starts a clean ephemeral session with neutral home/config roots; native agent configuration is disabled or explicitly selected, digest-bound, and untrusted.

For configured agent execution, consumer_managed is the default funding route and provider_sponsored_lumyn_managed is optional; credential owner and usage-billing owner are explicit and provider payment grants no code, context, session, or credential access.
Agent Runner Vendor and Model Provider are separate recorded roles, and no adapter, model, endpoint, credential-owner, or billing-owner fallback is silent.
One Provider Change Contract is confirmed once; each non-executable provider event binds its exact digest, audience, deadline, and supersession state.

A revocable Consumer Installation binds repository, action, agent_execution_policy, conditional Agent Runner/model-data, GitHub, retention, and disclosure policy; event authorization may narrow but never widen it.
Agent Runner/model request disclosure, endpoints/network, credentials, context, tools, budgets, funding, billing, and provenance are exact and separately authorized.
Agent output and self-reported tests are generation evidence; deterministic verification is independent and binds the exact candidate head.
Provider status is event-bound and consumer-consented; silence is unknown and merge is not retirement.

The generic-agent baseline holds repository/evidence, Agent Runner/model/auth/funding route, context, tools, commands, role, verification opportunity, and attempt/token/time/cost budgets constant; unmatched engine comparisons are descriptive.
There is no provider access to raw code, diffs, prompts, responses, agent sessions, tool traces, logs, or credentials, no default-branch write, and no auto-merge exception.

Agent Runner processes use explicit mounts, no host home, OS credentials, ambient sockets, or unrelated descriptors, inherited child restrictions, host-enforced egress, cleanup evidence, and no executable plugins, MCP servers, or hooks.

Independent verification uses a fresh exact-head view and separate process with frozen command/configuration digests, no Agent Runner or model credentials, and an evidence writer unavailable to generation.
Every product action freezes the exact route-selected capability union before action; unselected capabilities never become ambient authority.

`lumyn repair` is agent-assisted only: failed agent candidates reuse their bound route, while deterministic or imported-manual candidates require newly configured and explicitly authorized exact agent routes.

Local evidence, patch, optional local branch, and PR bundle remain fallback; first-campaign product proof requires one same run from authenticated provider event and installed preauthorization through an organically agent-assisted item on the consumer-selected qualified runner, independent exact-head verification, a tested Lumyn-opened draft PR, and a provider-received consented status projection; separate agent, delivery, or reporting runs do not qualify.

Managed Agent Runner credentials use one-time broker redemption into one quota-bound attempt session, allow multiple calls only within that attempt's hard quotas, forbid refresh, post-attempt replay, and cross-attempt reuse, and require revocation and reconciliation.
M1 is offline and deterministic-fake-only; M6 owns live adapter conformance/canaries and M10 owns the matched live baseline.

M2.5 qualifies consumer/runtime feasibility without claiming Lumyn adapter, host, or broker conformance before implementation; it also records a plausible organic agent-eligible item without forcing the route, and current qualification is mandatory immediately before the first live run.

M9 and M10 compose exact M4/M6/M7/M8/M9 action routes per installation and event; remote branch push and draft-PR creation remain atomic actions, delegated route semantics must match their sources, and campaign authority arrays are aggregate maxima, never ambient per-consumer grants.

Repository commands in M6-M10 use one fail-closed isolation contract for exact commands, directories, mounts, executable roots, neutral home/temp, environment, credentials, network, lifecycle scripts, child processes, budgets, and cleanup.

The provider campaign is a bounded five-unit attempt with a three-scan/two-outcome floor; credited readiness funds count only after non-refundable campaign conversion and total cleared funds reach $25,000.

The qualifying PILOT-003 proof is one composed run containing an organic agent-assisted plan item, draft PR, and provider-received status projection; deterministic rerouting cannot manufacture agent proof.
Campaign verdicts are pass or fail; reframe is only a post-failure disposition.

stop_conditions: factoryd dispatch is requested while the Factory profile or runtime remains unqualified
acceptance item is absent, unmapped, or closed only by milestone or slice
provider intent, consumer authority, model boundary, or redaction is ambiguous
prompt injection or untrusted content widens paths, tools, credentials, network, disclosure, or budget
generation self-verifies or verification does not bind the exact candidate head
provider code access, production credential, default-branch write, or auto-merge is requested
commercial evidence or generic-agent comparison is not direct, frozen, fair, and independently attested
